title: Mars water extraction thermodynamics, energy budget and microwave ISRU for OTA-TEC-0034
question: Source-grounded audit of OTA-TEC-0034: What does current primary/peer-reviewed/official Mars ISRU literature support for (1) water-ice sublimation/extraction under representative Mars pressures and temperatures, (2) useful heating/target-temperature ranges versus the dossier's provisional 0–20 °C assumption, (3) realistic process-energy ranges per kg or m³ of recovered water including heating, vapor capture and condensation/resublimation, and (4) the relative engineering merits and limitations of microwave in-situ heating versus excavation plus resistive/solar-thermal heating? Explicitly separate thermodynamic minima from system-level energy. Do NOT evaluate or rewrite the dossier's [F] 200–500 L/day gameplay/fiction placeholder or any NOXIA balancing value.
why_now: First OTA→NOXIA technical-object pilot; the dossier explicitly marks temperature, microwave efficiency and 15–40 kWh/m³ as unverified hypotheses that should be checked before technical canon is hardened.
real_world_anchor: Mars water-ice ISRU thermodynamics, sublimation, vapor capture, microwave/regolith heating and system energy studies.
novelty_reason: First source-pinned evidence audit of the water-extractor technical object.
